newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 9.5/10.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money edged up slightly to 9.5/10.0 percent from an opening of 8.5/9.0 percent on Tuesday morning, dealers said.
They said the overnight rate firmed slightly in mid-morning, possibly due to weekly tax payments due Tuesday.
One Japanese bank dealer said however, overall liquidity condition remained ample and longer-term rates were soft.
Dealers said early central bank injection of more than one trillion rupiah seemed to keep the market flushed. They said the ample supply was expected to sustain until the weekend.
The central bank had offered overnight papers (SBIs) at eight percent to limit declines of the overnight rate.
Swap rates were also soft, reflecting the ample condition.
One- and three-month money were quoted at around 13.50 and 14.875 percent, respectively.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 10.66 percent against 9.4 percent on Friday.
